newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ivorian coffee crop "at least" 200,000 T - premier.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian coffee crop "at least" 200,000 T - premier.

text.p: Ivorian Prime Minister Daniel Kablan Duncan said on Thursday that he expected the country's coffee crop to total at least 200,000 tonnes in 1996/97, up from around 170,000 tonnes last season.
"Coffee production will be higher than last year," Duncan told Reuters after speaking at a conference organised by the Club de Bruxelles.
"Cocoa prices are...alright...but coffee prices are not good and it's important for the economy that they improve," he added.

The expected improvement in Ivorian coffee output follows a 32 billion CFA revival plan, favourable crop weather and better maintenance of coffee plantations. -Peter Blackburn, Brussels Bureau +322 287 6830
